testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained correctly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: If you use spring brakes while carrying a heavy load, stopping will:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. If spring brakes activate because air pressure is low, your vehicle needs more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: Brake fade happens when:
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they overheat. This causes them to fade and work less effectively.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you should:

options.text: Set the parking brake only if parked on a slope.
Let 10 percent of the air out of the tires.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: If spring brakes are on, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. This could damage the brakes by combining spring force and air pressure.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used to:

options.text: Charge brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can temporarily release spring brakes if air pressure is low. Using the proper control lets the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into storage tanks. It stops pumping when pressure is too high and starts pumping when pressure is too low.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Reduce a vehicle's normal braking power.
Add to other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
Do not work well on large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add to other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works together with your normal braking system and does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS only activates when wheels are about to lock.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls this valve.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning comes on, you should:

options.text: Keep driving, but repair the brakes within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on while driving, stop the vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes. Check and repair the brakes right away.

questions.question: ABS can work on a vehicle if it is on:
questions.explanation: Even with anti-lock brakes on just one axle, you have better braking control than having no anti-lock brakes at all.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Does not work with air brakes.
Does not help in most driving situations.
Helps you stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS works with air brakes and helps drivers stay in control by preventing the wheels from locking up.

questions.question: When air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Start pumping air into the tanks.

questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when tanks reach about 125 psi. This level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share the brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle parked:

options.text: Only use the parking brake on hills.
Do not use the parking brake as it can damage tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parking. However, do not use it if brakes are very hot or if brakes are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: Brakes that are out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to work too hard and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to work too hard and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes that are out of adjustment fail faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent problems.

questions.question: Front wheel brakes work:
questions.explanation: Front wheel brakes work well in all road conditions, including ice. Front wheel skids are unlikely.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the air leakage rate should not exceed ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test for a triple combination vehicle, air should leak no more than 5 psi per minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What is removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If these build up in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what do both systems share?
questions.explanation: Both systems share a single air compressor. If it is damaged, neither system will work.

questions.question: Using brakes creates heat. If too much heat is produced, what happens?

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes can handle a lot of heat, but too much heat causes brake fade. This means the brakes lose their stopping power. Drivers should use engine braking too, not just the brakes alone.

questions.question: The ____ turn on when you push the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When you push the brake pedal, an electric switch turns on the brake lights. This tells other drivers that you are braking.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you more control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if ABS is on only one part of your vehicle, it still helps you control the vehicle better when braking. Brake normally when you have ABS.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil. These can damage the brake system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and oil.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has two separate air brake systems that use the same controls.
Is one air brake system with two different sets of controls.
Has one system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems that use the same controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems that share one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the front brakes, and the other controls the rear brakes.
